memo.verdict: Park. Do not progress COLO.B-DK to Early-Stage Assessment this cycle. Place on an active reassessment watchlist, not a hard drop. Trigger: a credible, numbers-attached strategy update from new CEO Gavin Wood (due at the close of his 90-day listening tour, landing almost exactly at memo date) or the Q3 FY25/26 results print, whichever comes first. This memo's park decision agrees with, and is substantially driven by, the risk-family report's own explicit stage-progression verdict: "the final recommendation is to Park the investment" until Gavin Wood's strategy update lands. The risk report's Analysis-of-Competing-Hypotheses matrix names FALSE FRIEND the winning hypothesis, with only two disconfirming items against ten for the bull case and three for the bear case. This is sequencing, not post-hoc justification: the risk report was read at the outset and carried through Element E8 RA8, the Section B BLUF, and this recommendation. Full reassessment criteria: (1) Gavin Wood's numbers-attached strategy update; (2) Kerecis inpatient growth holding double digits while outpatient stabilises above the source's own 0% quarterly warning threshold; (3) Luja catheter penetration tracking above the source's own 15% quarterly warning threshold; (4) a materially fresher risks-family report reaffirming or revising the false-friend ACH finding, since the current one predates Gavin Wood's public commentary.
case: Coloplast is a high-quality chronic-care compounder mid-way through a self-inflicted credibility reset, and the underlying business-quality case is corroborated across all four family reports without material contradiction. Core Chronic Care demand is genuinely non-discretionary (over 90% publicly reimbursed) and Core Chronic Care (Ostomy and Continence, roughly 68% of sales) kept growing 7-8% organically through the reset. Change forces are unambiguously present at scale on both axes (E1.RA1, B): externally, the Medicare outpatient reimbursement cap eradicated Kerecis's near-term economics, and the 2028 competitive-bidding expansion looms; internally, a full CEO transition, Impact4 re-basing and a manufacturing-footprint shift toward Portugal and Costa Rica are all running concurrently. A genuine offsetting tailwind exists too: new US reimbursement codes for hydrophilic catheters (active from 1 January 2026) accelerate premium conversion for the Luja platform, and the global population aged over 65 is projected to grow from 0.8bn to 1.9bn by 2060 — a durable secular demand tailwind.

The change-from-current magnitude clearly clears the bar (E1.RA2.CQ4, B): a 30% price-target compression, a full leadership reset, and a multiple that has fallen to 15x from a five-year peak of 32x — one of the largest de-ratings in the reviewed peer set. Bernstein Research frames a scenario where "restoring the historical 35x P/E premium could materialise if the MariGen transition outperforms the outpatient price cap." The primary fitting setup at Element E8 is "change-from-current clearing in a high-quality compounder" (RA4, B): six of nine sub-questions clear or partially clear, including the two most defining ones (investment phase — Portugal capex, MariGen transition costs against a stated mid-term recovery target; and high quality on a mid-term basis — sector-leading gross margin, dominant category shares, extreme patient switching costs all still intact through the reset). This fit is unusually clean for a Triaging-stage case versus cohort peers Smith & Nephew and Med-Kite, neither of which is mid-way through as sharp a leadership-and-portfolio reset. A secondary, incomplete setup fit also exists: "huge change-from-current clearing event in solid quality" (RA5, C) — all six covering brokers cut price targets in the same week (13-18 May 2026), a genuine synchronised reset, though not yet kitchen-sinked since Gavin Wood declined to reset guidance further.

Governance and accounting checks read clean (E8.RA7, B): no evidence of accounting fraud, zero material weaknesses or restatements, 39 of 40 governance recommendations met, an orderly (not distress-driven) 26-year PwC-to-EY auditor rotation, and zero activist-investor representations over the last twelve months. Thematically, Coloplast maps closely onto the active bear-market beneficiary profile (E5.RA1, B): non-discretionary demand, over 90% reimbursement coverage, and family-controlled ownership providing capital-allocation stability through a downturn; once placed on a brand in hospital, over 90% of patients remain loyal for 10 to 30 years, a subscription-like revenue pattern. The quality half of the E8.RA4 setup — 68% gross margin, 90% patient retention, triopoly market structure — is not in dispute anywhere across the four family reports; the genuine open question the memo carries forward is timing, not quality. Because the underlying business quality is real and not in dispute, the recommendation is park with a named reassessment trigger, not a permanent removal from the pipeline or universe: a stock with Coloplast's category-share, gross-margin and patient-switching-cost profile is uncommon in the universe screen, and a park driven by a leadership-transition-and-regulatory-shock timing problem, not a structural quality problem, does not warrant losing coverage.
counter_case: The risk-family report's own Analysis-of-Competing-Hypotheses matrix names FALSE FRIEND — apparent stability masking real deterioration — the winning hypothesis, with only two disconfirming evidence items against ten for the bull case and three for the bear case, and states directly: "the final recommendation is to Park the investment" until Gavin Wood's strategy update concludes. Two named mechanisms drive this: (1) apparent margin expansion masking R&D decay (the report's own Failure 9) — near-term operating margins hold near 26-28% while R&D spending stays flat at 4% of sales, well below the 6-8% medtech peer average; and (2) earnings beats potentially driven by channel stuffing (Failure 10) — rising receivables and distributor inventory are the named early-warning indicators, with net working capital held at 25% of sales in Q2 2025/26 versus a peer median of 22%, a 300bp gap kept live rather than resolved. A second, independently-sourced report (the developments-family tearsheet) corroborates the same pattern directly: "strong inpatient growth in Kerecis... a false friend that can mask ongoing structural decline." The risk report's own pre-mortem estimates a 20% false-friend scenario density across its full failure-mode set. Thin counter-evidence exists (free cash flow to sales improved to 20% in H1 2025/26 from 15% a year earlier) but the report itself warns this metric can be flattered by working-capital timing rather than organic demand.

Delivery has not been congruent with the thesis investors were sold — the single weakest sub-question in Element E1 (RA2.CQ3, F). Five independent evidence lines converge: guidance missed in three consecutive periods (FY24/25 guided 8-9%, delivered 7.00%; Q1 FY25/26 guided ~7%, delivered 6.00%; Q2 FY25/26 guided 6.50% consensus, delivered 6.00%); the change-forces digest itself classifies management as an "over-promiser" archetype; consensus three-year forward EPS expectations have fallen 600bp since 2023 versus a typical medtech peer decline of only 100-150bp (or 150-200bp, both source figures preserved); return on invested capital diluted from over 45% in FY2018/19 to just 15% in FY2024/25, "an extraordinary 700 basis-point decline" against a peer median decline of 150-200bp; and Kerecis organic growth fell to 0.00% against an initial 25-30% three-year compound-growth expectation set at acquisition.
triggers: - Has the guidance-cut sequence actually stopped? Not yet confirmed. Two consecutive cuts on record; Gavin Wood declined to comment, calling it "too early." Treat as unresolved until the strategy update lands.

- Is the false-friend guardrail (E8.RA8) a structural pattern or a single dated data point? Structural: flat R&D spend, receivables/working-capital signals, and independent corroboration from the developments-family report all converge. Monitor quarterly: trade-receivables ageing and distributor inventory levels (channel-stuffing mechanism); R&D spend as % of sales for any move toward the 6-8% peer average (R&D-decay mechanism).
- Does Gavin Wood's strategy update address the false-friend guardrail's two named mechanisms explicitly? Silence on R&D intensity and channel economics would itself be a soft negative signal.
- Kerecis inpatient growth: track against the source's own 0% quarterly warning threshold.
- Luja catheter penetration: track against the source's own 15% quarterly warning threshold.
- Track the 2028 competitive-bidding rulemaking process for early signal on final scope or magnitude of the pricing cut.
